turns.content: I want to start running but I've never really done it consistently. Any tips?
The biggest mistake beginners make is going too fast too soon. Start with a run-walk interval plan — something like 90 seconds running, 2 minutes walking, for 20 minutes.
How often should I run per week?
Three times a week is ideal to start. It gives you recovery time and makes it sustainable without burning out.
Should I invest in proper running shoes?
Yes, genuinely. Go to a running specialty store and get fitted — they'll watch you walk and recommend shoes for your gait. It makes a real difference for injury prevention.
What about nutrition — should I eat before a run?
For runs under 45 minutes, most people are fine with whatever they ate earlier. If you're running first thing in the morning, a banana 30 minutes before is enough.
How do I know if I'm running too fast?
The talk test — you should be able to hold a conversation without gasping. Easy runs should feel almost embarrassingly slow. Most people run their easy runs way too hard.
I keep getting shin splints. Any advice?
Usually a sign of too much too soon, worn-out shoes, or overstriding. Try shortening your stride, increasing your cadence, and adding a rest day. Ice after runs and calf stretching help too.
What's a realistic goal for a first-time runner?
A 5K without stopping after 8–10 weeks of consistent training is very achievable. Couch to 5K (C25K) is a well-designed free program that gets thousands of people there every year.
Great, I'll try the C25K app. Thanks!
Go slow, be patient, and don't skip the rest days. Consistency beats intensity at this stage every time.
